sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Java 8 changed how Java developers write code. Lambdas and streams replaced verbose anonymous classes and for loops. Every Spring Boot project, every data pipeline, every modern API uses these features. A fresher who cannot write a stream pipeline or explain Optional will struggle in any real Java team.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
- **Lambda** = anonymous function: `(params) -> body`. Must target a **@FunctionalInterface** (one abstract method).
- **Stream pipeline**: `source → zero or more intermediate ops → one terminal op`. Streams are **lazy** — nothing runs until the terminal op.
- **Common intermediate ops**: filter, map, sorted, distinct, limit, flatMap. **Common terminal ops**: collect, forEach, reduce, findFirst, anyMatch, count.
- **Optional** = a box that either holds a value or is empty. Use `orElse`, `orElseGet`, `map`, `filter` instead of null checks.
- **Method references** are shorthand for lambdas: `String::toUpperCase` = `s -> s.toUpperCase()`.
- **Default methods** let interfaces have concrete implementations without breaking existing implementations.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
- **lambdas-basics**: Know the three forms: no-param `() -> ...`, one-param `x -> ...`, multi-param `(x, y) -> ...`.
- **functional-interfaces**: Memorize Predicate<T> (test), Function<T,R> (apply), Consumer<T> (accept), Supplier<T> (get).
- **streams-basics**: Understand lazy evaluation — intermediate ops build a recipe; only the terminal op triggers execution.
- **optional-api**: Never call get() without isPresent() — use orElse or orElseThrow instead.
- **method-references**: Know all four types; the constructor reference `ClassName::new` appears frequently.
- **default-static-interface-methods**: Know that diamond problem with default methods is resolved by the implementing class overriding the method.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- *"What is the difference between map() and flatMap() in streams?"* — map transforms each element 1-to-1; flatMap transforms and flattens nested structures.
- *"What is lazy evaluation in streams?"* — Intermediate ops are not executed until a terminal op is encountered, enabling short-circuit optimization.
- *"What is a functional interface?"* — An interface with exactly one abstract method; lambdas are syntactic sugar for implementing it.
- *"Why is Optional better than returning null?"* — Optional forces the caller to handle the absent case explicitly, preventing NPE.
- *"What is the difference between orElse() and orElseGet()?"* — orElse() always evaluates the default; orElseGet() is lazy (only calls supplier if empty).

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"A stream pipeline in Java 8 works lazily — you chain filter, map, and other intermediate operations to describe what you want, and only when you call a terminal operation like collect or forEach does Java actually traverse the data source."*
